definitions.explanation: the act of stepping in place without moving forward, as in marching
a state where no progress is made despite continued effort

examples.japanese: ⟦{行進|こうしん}→行進：22196_koushin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To mark time during a march.

examples.japanese: ⟦{運動会|うんどうかい}→運動会：03013_undoukai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We practiced marching in place for the sports day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{寒波|かんぱ}→寒波：12354_kanpa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{温|あたた}めた→温める：02096_atatameru⟧。
examples.english: I warmed my body by stepping in place during the cold snap.

examples.japanese: ⟦{景気|けいき}→景気：02694_keiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧だ。
examples.english: The economy is in a state of stagnation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The negotiations are at a standstill.

examples.japanese: ⟦{売上|うりあげ}→売上：04102_uriage⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。

notes:
{足踏|あしぶ}み literally means stepping in place without moving forward. The figurative sense of stagnation or standstill is very common, especially in news and business contexts.

FORMS:
⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧ (foot) + ⟦{踏|ふ}む→踏む：01197_fumu⟧ (to step). Written as a compound noun.

VERB USAGE:
- {足踏|あしぶ}み⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to mark time; to stagnate)
- {足踏|あしぶ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧ (to continue stagnating)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足踏|あしぶ}み⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧ (state of stagnation)
- ⟦{景気|けいき}→景気：02694_keiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み (economic stagnation)
- ⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{足踏|あしぶ}み⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (negotiations stall)

REGISTER:
The literal sense (marching in place) appears in physical activity contexts like ⟦{運動会|うんどうかい}→運動会：03013_undoukai⟧. The figurative sense is more formal, common in news reporting and business discussions.
